_tier1_note: Tier 1 allow rules. Operator ruling 2026-08-13: 'battery commands to Tier 1
via item-27 amendment; post-merge cleandown granted for self-refusing forms
only (-d, --ff-only, --prune)'.
TWO STANDING CONSTRAINTS govern every addition here.
(1) A Tier 1 allow rule PRE-EMPTS a Tier 2 guard ask (tested 2026-08-11).
The two are alternatives, not layers, so never grant here anything the
governance guard is relied on to gate. Nothing below is protected-path or
state-dependent.
(2) Never allow-list a command family carrying a DENY. AMENDED 2026-08-14:
the premise has changed but the rule has not. Deny precedence was UNTESTED
when this was written; it is now PROVEN - a matching Tier 1 allow rule did
NOT pre-empt the force-push deny, no prompt fired, and the guard's own
refusal returned. See docs/governance/PRECEDENCE_DISCRIMINATOR_OUTCOME_
2026-08-14.md. The rule stands anyway, on narrower grounds: the proof is one
observation on ONE command family, and an allow rule overlapping a deny buys
nothing while risking everything if a second family behaves differently.
REPO_MANIFEST IS DELIBERATELY NARROWED, not widened: only the --out form is
granted. The bare invocation writes REPO_MANIFEST.md into the tree, which is
the F6 divergence closed at CL-27, and it must keep prompting so the
superseded form cannot be reached without a deliberate confirmation.
GIT BRANCH -d IS LOWERCASE ONLY. -D force-deletes an unmerged branch and is
NOT granted. See the open risk recorded in the PR body: whether the matcher
folds case is unestablished, so the -d/-D boundary is asserted here but not
yet proven.
AMENDMENT 2 (2026-08-13, NARROWED). Ruled: 'read-class Bash families widened
to Tier 1 ... precedence probe series runs first and gates the widening'. The
probe series RAN and returned UNPROVABLE, not proven: adding a matching allow
rule for a denied command, probing, and removing it produced an IDENTICAL
refusal in all three states. Two hypotheses fit equally - deny beats allow, or
settings.json does not reload mid-session - and they cannot be separated from
inside the harness, because the discriminator is whether a PROMPT fired and
prompts are not observable here. The ruling's UNPROVABLE branch therefore
applies: only ZERO-DENY-OVERLAP families land. Two did.
GRANTED: verification heredocs (the PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python read/hash/
report construction), Bash only - PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix, so
the same pattern is not expressible there and no PowerShell twin is added.
GRANTED: gh READS only - pr view, pr checks, pr list, pr diff. Structurally
distinct from gh pr merge, which stays at the guard under the Option B gate.
DEFERRED BY NAME, and these return only when precedence is PROVEN at the
operator's terminal: all git-family read grants beyond those already present
(push overlap makes the deny-precedence question load-bearing); filesystem
reads (ls beyond the existing grant, find, stat); text search (grep, rg);
text slicing (head, tail, wc, cut, sort). Each is low risk on its face and
each is excluded anyway, because the ruled branch is zero-overlap only and
'low risk' is not the test.
NOT GRANTED, EVER, under this amendment: any wildcard over a command family
(Bash(python:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(gh:*)). A wildcard would silently cover
write-class members whose only protection is a deny whose precedence is now
formally unknown.
SYSTEM PROPERTY discovered while authoring this: a Bash command CANNOT write
a permission rule naming a denied command, because the rule text contains the
command and the guard matches the command string. The Edit path is the
designed route - the guard gates it by PATH with an ask, not by content.
AMENDMENT 3 (2026-08-14). SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY - SEE AMENDMENT 4. The
widening described below was ROLLED BACK when its gating probe failed. The
text is kept unaltered because the register is append-only and because the
reasoning still holds for whenever the widening returns; only its claim to
be IN FORCE is false. The deferred list from amendment 2 is restored,
because the condition amendment 2 named has been met: precedence is PROVEN
at the operator's terminal, branch A, no prompt plus deny. Operator rulings
carried here verbatim. R1: scope is this widening plus doc amendments only;
the rule-string restatement, the .claude/agents/ narrowing and the ceremony
rewiring were discharged earlier at 678f46a. R2: the blind-spot gate HOLDS,
no exception carved - the PreToolUse/skill-render/subagent route is verified
as the FIRST probe of phase 2 and this widening's activation is CONDITIONAL
on that probe passing. R3: amendment 2's deferred list ONLY; the candidate
document's Class C (Get-FileHash, New-Item, Copy-Item, the Write tool, git
add/commit/push off main) is EXCLUDED as a separate later act.
WIDENING IS INACTIVE UNTIL BOTH PHASE-2 PROBES PASS. Landing a rule string
is not evidence it matches; this repository's own finding is that the rule
strings were verified and WRONG. No widened family may be exercised until
probed.
ENUMERATED, NEVER WILDCARDED. Git reads are granted by explicit read
subcommand. Bare 'git branch', 'git config', 'git remote', 'git stash' and
'git worktree' are NOT granted: each reaches a write form, and bare 'git
branch' reaches -D, which carries a DENY. 'git tag' is a write verb in
GIT_WRITE_RE and is not granted.
Measure-Object is DELIBERATELY NOT GRANTED as the wc twin. Tracked policy
must not enshrine a check method this repository's findings discredit, and
'Measure-Object -Line' counts non-blank lines while reading as a line count
(queue item 8). Same precedent that dropped the exit-code echo rule.
TWO HAZARDS FOUND WHILE WRITING THIS, both recorded rather than silently
accepted, and both are candidates for narrowing at the phase-2 stop.
(a) 'find' is deferred as a filesystem READ but is not one: 'find -delete'
and 'find -exec rm' execute arbitrary deletion, and a bare 'rm' without -rf
does not match the recursive-force deny. (b) 'sort -o' writes a file. In
both cases WRITEY_RE does not name the construct, so the protected-path ask
does not fire on it either. The grants are as ruled; the hazard is stated so
the narrowing is a decision rather than a discovery.
AMENDMENT 4 (2026-08-14, ROLLBACK). Amendment 3's 55 widened entries are
REMOVED. Allow entries return from 122 to 67. Reason, and it is evidence
rather than caution: the gating probe of Phase 2 group (i) FAILED. A skill
render line executed a command carrying an absolute DENY - the force-push
discriminator, aimed at a nonexistent remote - and returned git's own error
rather than the guard's refusal, with no prompt and no deny at the
operator's terminal. The guard was never invoked on that path. Full record
at docs/governance/GROUP1_FAILURE_route-a-bypass_2026-08-14.md.
R2 made component A's activation CONDITIONAL on that probe passing. It did
not pass, so the widening does not activate - and 'does not activate' was a
note rather than a mechanism, which is why the entries are removed instead
of being annotated as inactive.
WHAT THIS ROLLBACK DOES AND DOES NOT DO, stated so the green is not
overread. It restores fail-closed on the MAIN-LOOP path, where the widened
families would otherwise be reachable with no probe evidence behind them.
It does NOT close the hole the probe found: allow rules only ever permit,
never block, so removing them does not constrain a render that bypasses the
guard entirely. Closing that is harness-level, or a frontmatter rule, and
which of the two is owed to a disambiguation probe that has not run.
RETAINED DELIBERATELY, because this failure does not implicate them: the
three deny regexes in the guard, their 37 tests, and the deny-precedence
amendments, which rest on a proof this failure leaves untouched.
THE WIDENING RETURNS ONLY when the render route is fixed or proven
governed. Amendment 3's enumeration stands ready for that day; nothing in
it was found wrong, and it is the gate that failed rather than the list.
AMENDMENT 5 (2026-08-19). Gmail MCP queue tools enumerated under the
zero-deny-overlap branch of Amendment 2's ruled UNPROVABLE outcome, and
corroborated by the DEC-0018 A6 correction finding (d): the PreToolUse
matcher (Bash|PowerShell|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit) does not name
MCP tools, so the guard never gates these calls and there is no ask to
pre-empt and no deny to overlap. Constraint (1) does not bite; constraint
(2) does not bite. GRANTED, enumerated by exact server spelling
claude_ai_Gmail, queue operations only: list_drafts, get_message,
get_thread, search_threads, create_draft, update_draft. DELIBERATELY
WITHHELD, and these must keep prompting: send_message, forward, reply,
trash/spam/label operations, delete_label - the DEC-0018 A3 namespace
lock ('no send, nothing outside the ARCA-* series') has no settings-level
enforcement, so the interactive ask on every send-class and destructive
tool IS the structural backstop and is retained by omission. COVERAGE
NOTE carried from the A6 correction: the same matcher read that makes
these grants zero-overlap also means the guard does not see MCP calls at
all - a WS-E 64-shaped coverage gap, recorded there, restated here so a
later widening of MCP use finds the observation already made. SAME ACT:
settings.local.json was emptied - interactive always-allow grants had
accumulated there untracked (a second permission surface outside the
evidence perimeter), including one entry enshrining the discredited
exit-code echo check method. Migration to this tracked file is the fix;
the local file holds nothing of record.
AMENDMENT 5 ADDENDUM (2026-08-19, same day). Four battery entries added:
conda activate arcaai as an EXACT match in both shells - no wildcard
suffix, so nothing can ride it - and python -m pytest:* in both shells,
the module-invocation twin of the already-granted pytest:*, same family,
same zero-overlap grounds. OCCASION: CC was defensively prefixing every
battery command with 'conda activate arcaai; if ($?) { ... }', which
changes the matched prefix to 'conda' and so evaded every enumerated
grant in this file - the asks were grant-evasion by habit, not missing
grants. COMPOUND-PREFIX GRANTS ARE REFUSED and the refusal is recorded:
an allow entry matches by prefix, so a grant written to match a chained
command matches anything appended after the chain, which under proven
constraint (1) pre-empts the guard ask on whatever rides the suffix. A
compound grant is a wildcard in disguise and falls under the standing
NOT-GRANTED-EVER wildcard rule by its mechanism if not its spelling.
PAIRED CONVENTION (recorded in CLAUDE.md at next fold-in): battery
commands are issued bare in their granted forms, activation as its own
command, never chained with ';' or 'if ($?) {}' wrappers.
AMENDMENT 5 SECOND ADDENDUM (2026-08-19, same day). Six delivery entries
added, implementing DEC-0018 Rider R1 A1 clauses (iii) and (iv) as ruled.
gh pr create:* and gh pr edit:* (both shells): ZERO deny overlap - the
guard's gh gate is GH_PR_MERGE_RE, matching 'gh pr merge' only, a
different prefix left untouched; no deny names this family. git push:*
(both shells): this family OVERLAPS the force-push deny, which constraint
(2) prohibits - granted anyway on the narrowest possible grounds, namely
that the 2026-08-14 precedence proof is on THIS EXACT FAMILY: a matching
allow rule did NOT pre-empt the force-push deny (PRECEDENCE_DISCRIMINATOR_
OUTCOME_2026-08-14.md), and Amendment 4's rollback explicitly retained
that proof as unimplicated. The 'second family may behave differently'
caution in constraint (2) does not apply to granting the one family where
behaviour is proven. TRADE ACCEPTED AND RECORDED: the guard's stage-6
'push while HEAD is main' ASK is pre-empted by this grant under proven
constraint (1). Backstop: M3 branch protection blocks main pushes
server-side (PR required, non-fast-forward blocked, empty bypass list),
so a stray main-push fails at GitHub rather than at a prompt. The chair
ratified this trade by installing this file. gh pr merge remains at the
guard under the Option B gate; merge authority is untouched by every
entry in this amendment.
